_description: Hand-authored semantic notes for high-value UE 5.3 Material Functions. These notes complement the generated study index, which stores pins and node counts but not always human-readable formulas.
usage_rule: When explaining or using a Material Function, read generated metadata first, then check this file for function-specific formulas, caveats, and VFX usage notes.

functions.purpose: Fake velvet, moss, fuzz, or soft rim shading by darkening the facing core and brightening grazing angles.

inputs.Normal: Tangent-space normal input. Internally multiplied by float3(1, 1, TwoSidedSign) so two-sided/backface shading flips correctly.
inputs.CoreDarkness: Scalar controlling how much the camera-facing core darkens.
inputs.EdgeBrightness: Scalar controlling how bright the grazing/fuzzy edge becomes.
inputs.BaseColor: Vector3 color multiplied by the combined fuzzy shading factor.
inputs.Power: Scalar exponent controlling edge falloff sharpness. Higher values tighten the fuzzy rim.

outputs.Result: BaseColor multiplied by the fuzzy shading factor.

vfx_usage: Good for moss, velvet, fungus, fuzzy organic surfaces, cloth-like VFX meshes, and soft stylized rim shading.
For unlit/additive VFX, use Result as an emissive color or mask rather than expecting physically lit surface behavior.
For sprite flipbook fire/smoke, prefer ParticleSubUV, ParticleColor, DepthFade, and Fresnel first; use FuzzyShading only for mesh/surface looks.
caveats: The generated docs list pins and node counts only; this formula is hand-traced from get_material_function_info connections.
Do not simplify away TwoSidedSign when describing or rebuilding the function because it changes backface behavior.

functions.purpose: Compute falling-object World Position Offset and instantaneous velocity from current time, fall start time, and gravity acceleration.

inputs.Current Time: Scalar current time. Usually Time, particle age, or a material parameter.
inputs.Fall Start Time: Scalar time when the fall begins.
inputs.Gravitational Acceleration: Vector3 acceleration, typically cm/s^2. Earth-like UE gravity is usually float3(0, 0, -980).

outputs.Offset From Start Position: Vector3 displacement, commonly connected to World Position Offset.
outputs.Instantaneous Velocity: Vector3 velocity at the current elapsed time.

formula: Elapsed = clamp(Current Time - Fall Start Time, 0, 1)
Offset From Start Position = 0.5 * Gravitational Acceleration * Elapsed * Elapsed
vfx_usage: Good for shader-driven falling mesh pieces, fake debris sheets, leaves, cloth cards, or simple vertex animation.
For actual Niagara particles, prefer Niagara Gravity Force unless you specifically need material-side WPO.
caveats: The internal Clamp node defaults to 0..1, so elapsed fall duration is capped unless the function is edited.
Use cm/s^2 conventions when matching UE/Niagara gravity values.

functions.purpose: Generate a circular 2D spherical-height gradient in UV space. This is useful as a soft round mask, blob, decal falloff, impact center, shockwave core, or radial VFX mask.

inputs.UVs: Vector2 sample position in UV space. Defaults to TexCoord[0].
inputs.CenterPosition: Vector2 center of the sphere/circle in UV space.

outputs.Result 0-1: Normalized spherical height, 1 at the center and 0 at the radius edge.
outputs.Result Diameter: Unnormalized sphere thickness across the diameter at the sampled UV.
outputs.Result Radius: Unnormalized one-sided spherical height/radius at the sampled UV.

vfx_usage: Use Result 0-1 as an alpha mask for circular decals, soft impact spots, muzzle flash cores, portals, puddles, magic circles, or dissolve reveal centers.
Use Result Diameter or Result Radius when a material needs pseudo-volume thickness rather than just normalized alpha.
For simple linear radial masks, Distance/SmoothStep may be cheaper and more direct; use SphereGradient-2D when the spherical falloff shape matters.
caveats: The falloff is spherical/hemisphere-like, not linear. It stays fuller near the center and rolls off toward the edge.
If Radius is zero or extremely small, division can become unstable. Keep Radius above a small positive value.

functions.purpose: Generate a fresnel-like side falloff aligned to a chosen axis, especially useful for cylinders, beams, columns, and tube-like VFX where regular Fresnel is not the desired view response.

inputs.Axis: Vector3 axis to align against. Defaults to the mesh local Z axis transformed to world space. Keep it normalized for predictable results.
inputs.Normal: World-space normal used for the side/rim comparison. Defaults to VertexNormalWS.
inputs.Exponent: Scalar power applied to the fresnel result. Higher values make the rim tighter.

outputs.Fresnel: Axis-aligned fresnel mask with power applied.
outputs.Cylinder Thickness: Approximate ray travel distance through the side of an infinite cylinder; 1 means one cylinder diameter. It ignores cylinder end caps.

vfx_usage: Use Fresnel for cylinder side rims, energy columns, beams, shields, tube glows, vertical auras, and cylindrical forcefields.
Use Cylinder Thickness to fake volumetric density through a cylinder side, such as denser center and thinner edges for smoke, magic columns, or energy tubes.
This is stronger than normal Fresnel for cylinder materials because the response is constrained around a chosen axis.
caveats: This function does not handle cylinder caps; it is designed for the side surface.
If Axis is parallel or nearly parallel to the view direction, cross products can become unstable. The function is still useful, but extreme views may need clamping or art tuning.
Wire by target_input_name because Axis, Normal, and Exponent are easy to swap accidentally.
